newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end higher on Kia, sentiment weakens.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end higher on Kia, sentiment weakens.

text.p: Seoul stocks closed higher on Friday on hopes of an early settlement to the Kia crisis, but falling liquidity in the market kept investors sidelined, brokers said.
All six listed Kia firms went limit-up after Kia's announcement that Hyundai Motor and unlisted Daewoo Motor had agreed in principle to save Kia Steel, the most troubled unit of the Kia Group.
The composite index closed 5.33 points higher at 731.45.
"The deal between Hyundai, Daewoo and Kia brightened the future of Kia," said Kim Choon-kwon of Daewoo Securities.
Under the agreement, Hyundai, Daewoo and Kia Motors Corp would form a consortium to run Kia Steel. The three carmakers would have equal stakes in Kia Steel, Kia said.
Kia Motors rose 1,200 won to its daily limit of 16,300, and Asia Motors gained 370 won to 5,030. Kia Steel jumped 180 won to 2,500 and Kia Service rose 380 won to 5,210.
Shares of Ssangyong Motor also went limit-up on rumours that the upstart carmaker Samsung Motors would be interested in taking over Ssangyong, brokers said.
Ssangyong rose 360 won to its daily upper limit of 4,960.
Volume was relatively low at 28.98 million shares, compared with 25.83 million on Thursday. Gainers outpaced losers 531 to 225 with 136 stocks unchanged.
Brokers said low levels of customer deposits with securities houses, estimated at 3.03 trillion won against a yearly high of 3.6 trillion in mid-June, continued weighing on the market.
"The thin trading volume is because of falling liquidity," said Chung Chang-shik of Dongsuh Securities.

Brokers said sentiment improved briefly in the afternoon thanks to a report of shrinking trade deficit. The trade ministry said the customs-cleared trade deficit in July narrowed to $806 million from a $2.83 billion shortfall a year earlier.
